title: Assessing Rumination About Competition-Related Problems in Athletes
abstract: Abstract: The present project aimed to validate the State Sports Competition Rumination Scale (S-SCRS), a self-report measure designed to assess key characteristics of rumination – repetitiveness, intrusiveness, and uncontrollability – in athletes in relation to their current psychological state. The S-SCRS is a 3-item measure based on the original SCRS short form ( Michel-Kröhler, Krys, & Berti et al., 2025 ), with instructions adapted to capture current state rumination about competition-related problems. In two studies using data from 355 competitive athletes across various sports, construct validity was tested in terms of a multistate-single trait model and confirmed in a nomological network by negative correlations with self-compassion and positive correlations with depression, anxiety, stress, anger, and poor social support. In addition, reliability was examined in three stages with (1) nested alpha, (2) intraclass coefficients (ICCs), and (3) Spearman’s correlations for examining the score consistency over time. Results showed that the S-SCRS is fairly consistent but exhibits slight changes over time (ICC = .61). Additionally, a linear regression model confirmed that the S-SCRS is sensitive to competition performance. Overall, the S-SCRS appears to be a brief, reliable, and valid measure of state rumination about competition-related problems, suitable for use in future research and applied sport psychology.
